sources_considered.why: The September 2025 paper version reports full-task completion and failures in a simulated workplace.
Primary June 2025 evaluation measures completion and consistency in interactive customer-service tasks.
Independent measurements document both strong short-task performance and limitations on longer work; only the original dated findings are used.
Late-2025 developer claim of high reliability provides a relevant qualification for narrow workflows.
The original December 2024 results are outside the target period; a dated 2025 revision was used instead.
The 2026 study does not establish that its tested outcomes occurred within the target period.

receipt.public_excerpt: a majority of tasks are failed.

evidence_items.explanation: The 2025 evaluation reports 30.3% full completion for the best tested configuration, Gemini 2.5 Pro, across 175 workplace tasks. Its higher partial-credit score is not treated as successful completion.

evidence_items.locator: Section 4.2, Results, Impact of issue types
evidence_items.explanation: The telecom evaluation reports single-trial success around 34–50% for the tested agents and reduced consistency across repeated trials. This supports reliability limitations in interactive multistep work, with simulated users as a study limitation.

evidence_items.locator: Summary, discussion of current frontier capabilities
evidence_items.explanation: METR found near-perfect performance on tasks taking humans under four minutes, alongside much poorer results on longer tasks and rapid capability growth. This qualifies a blanket negative reading without establishing dependable general-purpose work.

Amazon reported high reliability in selected customer-built browser workflows before Marcus's post. This is material evidence against treating all agents as unreliable, but it is a developer claim about a narrower population than the contract.

unresolved_gaps: The studies do not constitute a representative census of all deployed agents.
No common reliability threshold makes the studies and developer claims directly interchangeable.
